speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of high fever, seizure, and a generalized nonpruritic rash; have you experienced any neck stiffness or severe headache alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hemorrhagic Edema of Infancy (AHEI). The clinical picture of a 9-month-old with a high fever, seizure, and a rapid onset of a non-pruritic, trunk-to-extremity rash is highly characteristic of this benign, self-limiting vasculitis. Given the patient's age and presentation, I am ruling out other causes like meningococcemia or Kawasaki disease, but the specific description of the rash spreading quickly without mention of purpura or mucosal involvement points strongly to AHEI. I will proceed with monitoring, as supportive care is the standard treatment.
